title.analysis: Authentic title "The First $100k is the Hardest (Why 75% Fail)" pairs a well-known Munger milestone with an unsourced failure percentage. Association only; no CTR or experiment evidence.

script.analysis: Full 19522 canonical characters read. A milestone explainer: Rolex/Tesla hook with "75%" statistic, savings by age, income vs wealth, lifestyle creep with raise arithmetic, payments mentality and car financing, assets vs liabilities, delayed-investing comparison, $100,000 threshold and Munger quote, compounding years 1-5, $1,000/month milestone ages, five-year delay cost, behaviour and optimisation traps, living-like-you're-broke, four steps (track, cut, automate, raise income), psychological stages and a close. Reproduces: car loan, $100K compounding, raise savings, take-home monthly. Overstated: $1.4M and $650K annuity results, $310K delayed balance (~$270K) and accelerating 3/2/1.5-year increments. Stale: $75,000 household income (2024 median $83,730). Unsourced: both "75%" figures. The stored ending is complete.
